fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (19x on ~$4.60 NTM non-GAAP EPS as of Sep-2027 = $87), FCF yield (5% on ~$4.35/sh FY28 FCF = $87) and EV/EBITDA (14x ~$3.2B FY28 EBITDA less ~$4.5B net debt = $74); weights 0.45/0.30/0.25 give ~$84.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) ~$4.60, from FY28 revenue ~$7.3B (+14% vs ~$6.4B FY27), op margin ~40-42%, interest ~$0.26B, tax ~13%, ~574M non-GAAP diluted shares; 19x multiple (mid of MCHP's historical 15-22x forward range, discounted for 5%+ 10-yr yields)

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~$2.4B (33% FCF margin, same as Q1 FY27's 33.5%) / ~550M shares = ~$4.35/sh; 5.0% required FCF yield

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 adj. EBITDA ~$3.2B (44% of $7.3B); 14x = $45B EV; less ~$4.5B net debt after continued paydown (LT debt $5.36B, cash $0.27B at Jun-2026, ~$0.4-0.5B/qtr excess FCF to debt) = $40.5B / 550M shares

bear.story: The 2026 booking surge turns out to be channel restocking plus pre-buying ahead of price increases; industrial/auto demand stalls in 2027, the one-off gross-margin boosts (licensing, reserve releases) fade, and the multiple compresses with 5%+ Treasury yields. NTM EPS ~$3.2 x 15.5x.

base.story: Recovery continues at a slower pace: FY28 revenue ~$7.3B, gross margin ~65-66%, op margin ~40%, data center/PCIe Gen6 ramps in 2027, and net leverage falls below 2.5x. NTM EPS ~$4.6 x 19x.

bull.story: A full cyclical upturn toward the FY23 peak (~$8.4B revenue, ~$6 EPS run-rate): price increases stick, the operating margin reaches the 45% long-term model, data center grows past $1.5B, buybacks restart, and the multiple re-rates to ~22x on ~$5.4 NTM EPS.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$55 (about -30%, near the 52-week low of $48.52 and ~13x current NTM EPS), the market would be pricing an outright reversal of the upturn: sequential revenue declines, a book-to-bill below 1, inventory days rising again, and gross margin falling back toward the low 60s. A fall that deep would most likely mean the restocking-driven recovery has ended, not ordinary 50%-vol noise.

catalysts.event: Q2 FY27 results and December-quarter guide (mgmt says better than the typical -3 to -5% seasonal decline; full-quarter price-increase benefit)
Q3 FY27 results; March-quarter guide; gross margin as the licensing and reserve benefits roll off
Q4 FY27 results and FY28 outlook; possible capital-return update once net debt/EBITDA is below 2.5x
Q1 FY28 results; PCIe Gen6 / NVMe data-center production ramps
Fed and Treasury-yield path (10-yr ~5.1%) and US-China tariff/trade negotiations
Hailo edge-AI integration (closed 2026-09-21) and possible further tuck-in M&A

key_uncertainties: Is the strongest bookings quarter in four years end demand or restocking/pre-buying before price increases?
Gross-margin sustainability after one-time licensing and inventory-reserve benefits; underutilization charges
Valuation multiple under 5%+ 10-yr yields and sector-wide semis de-rating (analog selloff since May-2026 high)
Foundry/OSAT advanced-packaging capacity constraints limiting data-center shipments
Pace of deleveraging vs. restart of buybacks; insider (CEO) 10b5-1 selling
Industrial and automotive recovery lagging data center and aerospace/defense
reasoning: Fundamentals are clearly improving. Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue was $1.485B (+38% y/y, +13% q/q), non-GAAP GM 63.8%, OM 35.1%, EPS $0.76 (beat). The Q2 guide is $1.59-1.62B and EPS $0.91-0.95. Bookings are the strongest in four years, book-to-bill is well above 1, inventory days fell to 175, a price increase is in place, and data center should reach ~$1B in CY26 (+69%). The CFO repeated all of this at Citi on 9-Sep-2026. The stock (close $78.69) nevertheless sits ~25% below its May high, driven by a sector-wide analog/semis de-rating, a 10-yr yield of ~5.1% and cycle-peak worries. That puts it at about 19x NTM EPS (~$4.2) and ~21.5x consensus FY27 EPS of $3.65. I model FY28 revenue of ~$7.3B and NTM EPS of ~$4.6 by Sep-2027, and value it at 19x P/E / 5% FCF yield / 14x EV/EBITDA, blended to ~$84 (plus ~$1.82 of dividends not in the price). The sell-side mean target of ~$100-108 looks optimistic given the rate backdrop. Scenarios are bear $50 (25%), base $88 (50%) and bull $120 (25%), for a mean of ~$86.5. For the ladder I used a lognormal centered on a ~$84 median with 40% sigma: below the 50% realized vol, which is inflated by macro/sector shocks, but wide enough for a cyclical name at an inflection. I fattened the left tail slightly for a cycle reversal. P(>= today's price) is ~0.56. Research was done with web search; no option data was consulted.
